verses.zh: （可拉后裔的诗，交与伶长。）万民哪，你们都要拍掌！要用夸胜的声音向　神呼喊！
verses.en: For the music director, by the Korahites; a psalm.All you nations, clap your hands.Shout out to God in celebration.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 47. In this hymn the covenant community praises the Lord as the exalted king of the earth who has given them victory over the nations and a land in which to live.

verses.zh: 因为耶和华至高者是可畏的；他是治理全地的大君王。
verses.en: For the Lord Most High[NOTE:1] is awe-inspiring;[NOTE:2] he is the great king who rules the whole earth![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Shout to God with [the] sound of a ringing cry!”
The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן, ʿelyon) pictures the Lord as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked.

Or “awesome.” The Niphal participle נוֹרָא (noraʾ), when used of God in the psalms, focuses on the effect that his royal splendor and powerful deeds have on those witnessing his acts (Pss 66:3, 5; 68:35; 76:7, 12; 89:7; 96:4; 99:3; 111:9). Here it refers to his capacity to fill his defeated foes with terror and his people with fearful respect.

verses.zh: 他叫万民服在我们以下，又叫列邦服在我们脚下。
verses.en: He subdued nations beneath us[NOTE:1] and countries[NOTE:2] under our feet.
notes: Heb “a great king over all the earth.”

On the meaning of the verb דָּבַר (davar, “subdue”), a homonym of דָּבַר (“speak”), see HALOT 209-10 s.v. I דבר. See also Ps 18:47 and 2 Chr 22:10. The preterite form of the verb suggests this is an historical reference and the next verse, which mentions the gift of the land, indicates that the conquest under Joshua is in view.

verses.zh: 他为我们选择产业，就是他所爱之雅各的荣耀。（细拉）
verses.en: He picked out for us a special land[NOTE:1] to be a source of pride for[NOTE:2] Jacob,[NOTE:3] whom he loves.[NOTE:4] (Selah)
notes: Heb “he chose for us our inheritance.” The prefixed verbal form is understood as a preterite (see “subdued” in v. 3).
Heb “the pride of.” The phrase is appositional to “our inheritance,” indicating that the land is here described as a source of pride to God’s people.

verses.zh: 神上升，有喊声相送；耶和华上升，有角声相送。
verses.en: God has ascended his throne[NOTE:1] amid loud shouts;[NOTE:2] the Lord has ascended amid the blaring of ram’s horns.[NOTE:3]
notes: Jacob whom he loves. The Lord’s covenantal devotion to his people is in view.

God ascended his throne. In the context of vv. 3-4, which refer to the conquest of the land under Joshua, v. 5 is best understood as referring to an historical event. When the Lord conquered the land and placed his people in it, he assumed a position of kingship, as predicted by Moses (see Exod 15:17-18, as well as Ps 114:1-2). That event is here described metaphorically in terms of a typical coronation ceremony for an earthly king (see 2 Sam 15:10; 2 Kgs 9:13). Verses 1-2, 8-9 focus on God’s continuing kingship, which extends over all nations.

Heb “God ascended amid a shout.” The words “his throne” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The Lord’s coronation as king is described here (see v. 8). Here the perfect probably has a present perfect function, indicating a completed action with continuing effects.

verses.zh: 你们要向　神歌颂，歌颂！向我们王歌颂，歌颂！
verses.en: Sing to God! Sing!Sing to our king! Sing!

verses.zh: 因为　神是全地的王；你们要用悟性歌颂。
verses.en: For God is king of the whole earth.Sing a well-written song.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the Lord amid the sound of the ram horn.” The verb “ascended” is understood by ellipsis; see the preceding line.

verses.zh: 神作王治理万国；　神坐在他的圣宝座上。
verses.en: God reigns[NOTE:1] over the nations.God sits on his holy throne.
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term also occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142. Here, in a context of celebration, the meaning “skillful, well-written” would fit particularly well.

verses.zh: 列邦的君王聚集要作亚伯拉罕之　神的民。因为世界的盾牌是属　神的；他为至高！
verses.en: The nobles of the nations assemble,along with the people of the God of Abraham,[NOTE:1] for God has authority over the rulers[NOTE:2] of the earth.He is highly exalted.[NOTE:3]
notes: When a new king was enthroned, his followers would acclaim him king using this enthronement formula (Qal perfect 3ms מָלַךְ, malakh, “to reign,” followed by the name of the king). See 2 Sam 15:10; 1 Kgs 1:11, 13, 18; 2 Kgs 9:13, as well as Isa 52:7. In this context the perfect verbal form is generalizing, but the declaration logically follows the historical reference in v. 5 to the Lord’s having ascended his throne.

The words “along with” do not appear in the MT. However, the LXX has “with,” suggesting that the original text may have read עִם עַם (ʿim ʿam, “along with the people”). In this case the MT is haplographic, having dropped one set of עם (ʿayin-mem). Another option is that the LXX is simply and correctly interpreting “people” as an adverbial accusative and supplying the appropriate preposition.

Heb “for to God [belong] the shields of the earth.” Perhaps the rulers are called “shields” because they are responsible for protecting their people. See Ps 84:9, where the Davidic king is called “our shield,” and perhaps also Hos 4:18.
